LESSON: INEQUALITIES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 1.6: Inequalities
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Inequalities, part of NUMBERS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you simplify algebraic expressions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Inequalities together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner develops self-drive as they individually and confidently work out simple inequalities

involving one unknown.

19

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes care of learning resources when simplifying algebraic inequalities and playing

digital games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Citizenship: The learner displays social cohesion as they work in groups to form algebraic inequalities that represent

different aspects of life within the environment.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner writes and simplifies inequalities to represent the amount of fertilizers and

other production inputs to be used on a school farm during agriculture projects.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Reference materials in Braille and appropriate print, Mathematics Braille primer,

place value apparatus with appropriate font and colour contrast, abacus, Taylor frames with plastic types or cubes and

cubarithm boards.
